hero.lead: A federation of seven emirates and 11.5 million residents, a global hub for trade and finance, where Abu Dhabi raised $5.5 billion in bonds in the first half of 2026 and the UAE will host the World Bank and IMF meetings in 2029.

register.name: Federal Treasury Bonds and Islamic Treasury Sukuk, 2026 calendar
register.detail: UAE Ministry of Finance · dirham auctions from 27 January 2026 · AED 11bn institutional and AED 150M retail in the 2026 calendar · AED 4.4bn redeemed in 2026 · AED 32.5bn outstanding on 6 November 2026
register.note: Budget-wide; in July, bids of AED 4.83 billion for AED 1.1 billion issued, an oversubscription of 4.4 times
register.text: Dirham bonds and Islamic sukuk of the federal government, sold at monthly auctions to institutions and, from 2026, to retail investors. They fund the federal budget as a whole and are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: TAQA blue bond (five years, 5.125%)
register.detail: TAQA Group · 30 July 2026 · five years · coupon 5.125% · private placement · rated Aa3 by Moody’s and AA by Fitch
register.note: The first Blue Bond under TAQA’s Green and Blue Finance Framework
register.text: A blue bond of TAQA Group, placed privately with international investors. Its net proceeds finance or refinance eligible blue projects under the framework, in a group that invests in desalination, water transmission and distribution, and wastewater treatment and reuse, which carry the water standard.

register.name: Round-the-clock solar and battery project, Abu Dhabi
register.detail: Masdar with the Emirates Water and Electricity Company · financial close 13 July 2026 · 5.2GW solar PV and 19GWh battery storage · 13 banks · US$1bn of equity from Masdar · operation expected in 2027
register.note: Total capital investment; the debt amount is not stated
register.text: Project finance from 13 international and local banks, among them First Abu Dhabi Bank, Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank, Dubai Islamic Bank and KfW IPEX-Bank, for a solar plant integrated with battery storage that Masdar calls the world’s first gigascale 24/7 clean energy project. It is being developed in Abu Dhabi and bears on the energy standard.

register.name: Abu Dhabi bond reopenings
register.detail: Department of Finance, Abu Dhabi · 15 April 2026 · US$1bn of 4.875% notes due 2029 and US$1.5bn of 5.0% notes due 2034
register.note: Budget-wide; each series now has US$3 billion outstanding
register.text: $1.5 billion of 5.0% notes due 2034 and $1 billion of 4.875% notes due 2029, added to existing bonds of the Government of Abu Dhabi under its global medium-term note programme. They fund the emirate’s budget as a whole and are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Abu Dhabi dual-tranche bonds
register.detail: Department of Finance, Abu Dhabi · 5 and 10 years · February 2026
register.text: The emirate’s first bond sale of 2026, a dual-tranche offering of five and ten years by the Government of Abu Dhabi. It funds the emirate’s budget as a whole and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Sheikh Zayed Housing Programme, housing decisions of 2025
register.detail: UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure · 3,567 decisions in 2025 · grants, government housing loans and housing financing with national banks · 759 more approvals worth AED 616M in the first quarter of 2026
register.note: More than 73,000 housing support decisions worth more than AED 50 billion since the programme began in 1999
register.text: Federal housing support for UAE citizens. In 2025 it issued 524 presidential grants worth AED 356.3 million, 623 government housing loans worth AED 270.2 million, 32 housing grants worth AED 25.4 million and 2,388 housing financing decisions worth AED 1.894 billion, which carry the shelter standard.
by: UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure

register.name: Abu Dhabi bonds of three and ten years
register.detail: Department of Finance, Abu Dhabi · 30 September 2025 · US$1bn due in three years and US$2bn due in ten years · 10 and 18 bps over US Treasuries · peak orders US$18.5bn
register.note: Budget-wide; the tightest spreads in Abu Dhabi’s history, the Department of Finance says
register.text: US dollar bonds of the Government of Abu Dhabi, five times oversubscribed. The Department of Finance says they secure a lower cost of capital for the strategic entities that drive the emirate’s growth; they fund the budget as a whole and are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Abu Dhabi housing projects for citizens
register.detail: Abu Dhabi Housing Authority and Abu Dhabi Projects and Infrastructure Centre · 24 September 2025 · 13 projects · 25,244 homes (AED 94bn) and about 14,876 residential plots (AED 12bn) · all due by 2029
register.note: Agreements with Aldar Properties, Bloom Holding, Modon Properties, Lead Development Real Estate and IMKAN Properties
register.text: Agreements with property developers for more than 40,000 homes and residential plots for Emirati citizens in Abu Dhabi city, Al Ain and Al Dhafra. The release gives the cost but not how it is financed; the homes carry the shelter standard.
by: Abu Dhabi Projects and Infrastructure Centre

register.name: Masdar green bond (five and ten years)
register.detail: Masdar · 16 May 2025 · two tranches of US$500M · 5 and 10 years · coupons 4.875% and 5.375% · 80 and 90 bps over US Treasuries · peak orders US$6.6bn
register.note: Masdar’s third green bond; US$2.75 billion outstanding under its green bond programme
register.text: A green bond of Masdar, the UAE clean energy company, whose proceeds go exclusively to greenfield renewable energy projects. The release does not say where the projects are; the line bears on the energy standard.

register.name: Currency swap between the dirham and the Bahraini dinar
register.detail: Central Bank of the UAE and Central Bank of Bahrain · signed 8 April 2026 · AED 20bn (BHD 2bn) · five years
register.note: Signed by the two governors at a virtual ceremony
register.text: A currency swap agreement between the UAE dirham and the Bahraini dinar, with a nominal value of AED 20 billion and a tenor of five years. The Central Bank of the UAE says it promotes the use of local currencies and strengthens trade and investment ties; it is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

enterprises.heading: Already working in the United Arab Emirates.

items.name: Peekabox
items.text: A Dubai start-up whose app sells end-of-day surplus food from more than 1,000 shops, among them Carrefour, Costa Coffee and Pret a Manger, at 50% to 70% below the retail price, to cut waste and ease the cost of living.

items.name: Platable
items.text: A Dubai app that turns surplus meals into steep discounts, with more than 200 outlets listing their surplus, over 1.5 tonnes of food rescued and about 30,000 people signed up in its first four months.

items.name: Jade
items.text: An SME from the UAE whose gamified platform screens children for neurodevelopmental conditions with cognitive assessments, eye-tracking and personalised learning; it is used in over 450 institutions in 179 countries, has supported more than 180,000 children and won the Health category of the Zayed Sustainability Prize in 2026.

items.name: Mawaheb
items.text: An art studio and café in Al Quoz, Dubai, that has supported people of determination since 2010 through art, life skills training and vocational programmes, with students aged 18 to 62, and serves specialty coffee and food to the public.

items.name: 21 Cafe
items.text: A café in Al Ghurair Centre, Deira, opened in April 2025 by a parent, where four young adults with Down syndrome support the baristas by serving coffee and cakes, with plans to grow into a chain.
